steps.description:
Using a table to plot out the different scenarios of a program is one of the techniques in designing a program. In this challenge, you will practise interpreting a table and converting the information into code.
You can join AND blocks as shown below to check multiple conditions. When ALL conditions are true, the combined result will be true.


Below is a table showing which button should be pressed when an obstacle is within a certain distance in order to produce a beeping sound.


Study the table and create a program such that only when the correct button is pressed, a beeping sound will be heard.

You can join AND blocks as shown below to check multiple conditions. When ALL conditions are true, the combined result will be true.


While you can chain multiple AND conditions, it's best to limit them to three for readability and easier debugging. You'll soon explore alternative methods for handling complex condition checks.

A biochemical team is conducting an experiment with the set up as shown below.

        

An Ultrasonic sensor is used to detect the chemical level. When the chemical reaches certain level, the scientists can hold down certain button(s) to release the chemical.
Below shows the action table.



Write a program to support this experiment. It will open the right gate when the conditions are met. Using the LCD, display the action whenever it occurs (e.g. "Open Gate A", etc).

You can join AND blocks as shown below to check multiple conditions. When ALL conditions are true, the combined result will be true.


While you can chain multiple AND conditions, it's best to limit them to three for readability and easier debugging. You'll soon explore alternative methods for handling complex condition checks.

In your previous step, you were a great help to the biochemical team by creating the code to enable them control the chemical level following the action table below.

        

However, the biochemical team feels that it can be improved by adding warning alarm. The following is what they suggest:

1. The program will keep checking the chemical level.

2. If the Ultrasonic sensor value is from 21 to 30, make a slow beeping until Gate A opened.

3. If the Ultrasonic sensor value is from 11 to 20, make a medium beeping until Gate B is opened.

4. If the Ultrasonic sensor value is from 0 to 10, make a fast beeping until both gates are opened. 

5. Show the action on the LCD whenever the button is held down to open the gate.
